algorithms.name: Bubble Sort
algorithms.description: Repeatedly steps through the list, compares adjacent elements and swaps them if they are in the wrong order.
algorithms.summary: Repeatedly swap adjacent out-of-order elements until the list is sorted.
algorithms.explanation: Bubble sort works by repeatedly swapping adjacent elements if they are in the wrong order. Each pass through the list places the next largest element in its correct position.
notes: Elements still in play are blue; the pair under comparison turns red and confirmed elements turn green.
The sorted suffix grows by one element after every full pass.
algorithms.steps_hint: One playback step = one adjacent comparison.

algorithms.name: Quick Sort
algorithms.description: Divide and conquer algorithm that picks an element as pivot and partitions the array around the pivot.
algorithms.summary: Pick a pivot, partition around it, then sort each side recursively.
algorithms.explanation: Quick sort selects a pivot element and partitions the array into two sub-arrays: elements less than the pivot and elements greater than the pivot. The process is recursively applied to the sub-arrays.
notes: The pivot turns yellow while the partition is being built, and each side is then sorted recursively.
Positions turn green once they have reached their final sorted place.
algorithms.steps_hint: One playback step = one partition comparison or pivot placement.

algorithms.name: Merge Sort
algorithms.description: Divide and conquer algorithm that divides the array into halves, sorts them, and merges them back.
algorithms.summary: Split the array into halves, sort each half, then merge them back in order.
algorithms.explanation: Merge sort divides the array into halves until each sub-array has one element, then merges them back together in sorted order. This is a classic divide-and-conquer algorithm.
notes: The runs currently being merged are purple and the elements being compared turn red.
Each level of the recursion doubles the length of the sorted runs.
algorithms.steps_hint: One playback step = one merge of a pair of runs.
